name: kingdom
description: Multi-agent orchestration kit for Claude Code — parallel AI coding with Git worktrees and native cmux.app. /kingdom:work runs the full daily cycle in one command. v0.35.0 completes the modular architecture: rules/ (one rule per file) + functions/ (42 *.sh + _load.sh) + roles/ (slim role specs) + reference/ + a manifest.json feature registry where `load_feature <name>` sources just that feature (so senior/watchman plug in or out with no edits to core), plus a structure-lint in /kingdom:self-care. Every file stays short and a run loads only what it calls. v0.33.0 simplified the command surface: /kingdom:init takes no flags (scaffold only), /kingdom:work shape is per-role (worker=/co-worker=/watchman=/senior=, plural accepted) or lane=N (King auto-composes a total budget), and pacing is two plain ceilings pr-limit=N and pod-limit=N (cap renamed, target removed). v0.32.0 added the Senior role (🎓 Opus) and story-pod integration branches: parallel workers on one story merge into a local story branch, reviewed as a unit by a Senior in an autonomous loop, then promoted as a single PR (three-tier gate; King owns cross-story, Senior owns within-story; R46-R50 + R30 delegated-dispatch). v0.31.1 fixes two consumer-reported bugs (claude REPL not auto-launching on worker spawn; King's poll loop calling a stale-named overlay function via the silent-no-op bash-function-missing path), adds R45 (Haiku-army doc orientation for all roles), watchman senior-dev review with doc cross-check, mandatory worker smoke-test reports, and Sonnet default for the sub-agent pool. v0.31.0 hardened R4/R9/R30/R36/R37 with bash-level gate helpers. A King (👑 Opus) coordinates generic workers (👷), co-workers (🧑‍💼), and watchmen (🕵️) — each in its own cmux.app workspace. Kingdom branch is a WORKING-TREE OVERLAY for review (never commit on kingdom). PRs carve from worker-N tip byte-for-byte. Two-tier gate. Domain-agnostic. Bootstrap with /kingdom:init; run the day with /kingdom:work; close with /kingdom:save. Won't touch your project files, develop/main branches, shell config, or git config.
